_comment: Service pairs: the Compose service and the chart component that runs the
same application. The parity gate (scripts/config-parity-check.py) compares
the environment both surfaces give that application.
Three categories, per service. Every entry carries the reason it is one —
an entry without a reason is a gap in disguise.
mayDiffer    : the chart sets the variable and its value is the
Kubernetes one — an address, a topology fact, or a
deliberate policy difference. The variable must still be
present: the application needs it on both surfaces.
composeOnly  : the variable only makes sense on the Compose surface.
notRead      : no code in the repository reads the variable.
A variable in none of the three must be configured the same way on both
surfaces — that is the parity this gate protects.

mayDiffer.ARANGO_DB: the chart's ArangoDB instance serves _system, ArangoDB's own database, which always exists; Compose uses a dedicated genie-ai database. Intentional divergence: moving an existing deployment means migrating every collection, not switching a value. The knob is data.arangodb.database (default _system)
mayDiffer.ARANGO_URL: in-cluster Service DNS instead of the Compose service name
mayDiffer.ARANGO_PASSWORD: carried by the arango-root-secret Secret the operator provides
mayDiffer.ENABLE_OBSERVABILITY: the chart's observability tier is an operator-enabled install of its own; Compose gates the same services behind a profile
mayDiffer.KEYCLOAK_URL: the backend resolves JWKS in-cluster; Compose reaches Keycloak through the public origin
mayDiffer.OPEA_HOST: in-cluster Service DNS instead of the Compose service name
mayDiffer.OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT: the collector is an operator-managed instance with its own Service name
mayDiffer.TRANSLATION_BACKEND: the chart names a translation API, and the application treats a named API as mandatory; Compose leaves the choice to the startup probe
mayDiffer.TRANSLATION_CACHE_HOST: in-cluster Service DNS instead of the Compose service name
mayDiffer.VICTORIALOGS_URL: the collector is an operator-managed instance with its own Service name
mayDiffer.VLLM_API_KEY: carried by the vllm-api-key Secret the operator provides
mayDiffer.VLLM_TRANSLATION_ENDPOINT: the chart points at the OPEA tier's endpoint (in-cluster Service or GPU node); Compose at its own guardrail service
mayDiffer.CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS: same allowlist intent, expressed with the deployment's public origin (ingress.host) instead of Compose's localhost list
mayDiffer.CSP_CONNECT_SRC: same policy intent, expressed with the deployment's public origin
mayDiffer.GPU_NODE_HOST: the chart names the GPU node it was configured with; Compose leaves it empty unless the remote-GPU topology is used

notRead.EMAIL_FROM: read by no service in the repository — the Keycloak convergence job is the only consumer of the EMAIL_* names, and it takes the password from a Secret
notRead.EMAIL_HOST: read by no service in the repository — see EMAIL_FROM
notRead.EMAIL_PORT: read by no service in the repository — see EMAIL_FROM
notRead.EMAIL_SECURE: read by no service in the repository — see EMAIL_FROM
notRead.EMAIL_USER: read by no service in the repository — see EMAIL_FROM
notRead.EMAIL_PASSWORD: read by no service in the repository — see EMAIL_FROM

codeDefault.MAX_MODEL_LEN_TEXTGEN: empty in Compose; the code reads 0 as 'not set' and falls back to its own limit, and the chart leaves it unset
codeDefault.MAX_TRANSLATION_CHARS: empty in Compose; the code reads 0 as 'not set' and falls back to its own limit, and the chart leaves it unset
codeDefault.MULTI_TURN_CONDENSE_SYSTEM_PROMPT: empty in Compose; the code falls back to its built-in rewrite prompt when the variable is unset, and the chart leaves it unset

composeOnly.LLM_SERVER_HOST_IP: Compose points these at its own vllm service name; the chart configures the endpoint form instead (VLLM_LLM_ENDPOINT), which the code parses into host and port before reading either variable, so leaving them unset yields the same endpoint. The chart never sets the name: the code derives the endpoint from the configured GPU endpoint (the parsed hostname overrides this fallback), so the compose service name only ever made sense on that surface.
composeOnly.LLM_SERVER_PORT: Compose points these at its own vllm service name; the chart configures the endpoint form instead (VLLM_LLM_ENDPOINT), which the code parses into host and port before reading either variable, so leaving them unset yields the same endpoint. The chart never sets the name: the code derives the endpoint from the configured GPU endpoint (the parsed hostname overrides this fallback), so the compose service name only ever made sense on that surface.

secretProvided.OPENAI_API_KEY: Compose maps `${VLLM_API_KEY:-}` into it (docker-compose.yaml); the chart delivers the same GPU key from the vllm-api-key Secret under that name — the translation and condense clients read only OPENAI_API_KEY for their Bearer header, and a GPU node enforcing the key would see 'Bearer None' without it.

codeDefault.VUE_APP_AVAILABLE_LOCALES: empty in Compose; the frontend treats an unset value as 'every locale available'
codeDefault.VUE_APP_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS: Compose leaves it empty (the env template line is commented) and the frontend entrypoint injects the empty value into the runtime config.js — the code default applies on both surfaces. The chart leaves it unset for the same result; a deployment that tunes it adds the env row to services.frontend.env.

mayDiffer.VUE_APP_CSP_CONNECT_SRC: the browser's origin is the deployment's public origin (ingress.scheme + ingress.host); Compose's list names the localhost development origins

notApplicable.VUE_PROXY_HOST: the chart serves the SPA and the API from the same origin, so the development proxy host is never dialled

composeOnly.PORT: The chart does not set the name at all: its Deployment carries the port as containerPort 8090 (services.frontend.port), and the frontend image's embedded nginx listens on that baked-in default — the PORT env only steers the compose-run process.

mayDiffer.ARANGO_URL: in-cluster Service DNS instead of the Compose service name

mayDiffer.EMAIL_FROM: the chart's convergence Job takes its SMTP settings from data.keycloak.smtp; its defaults are placeholders for a deployment with no SMTP, and Compose takes them from the root env file
mayDiffer.GENIE_ADMIN_EMAIL: the operator supplies it on both surfaces; the chart's value comes from data.keycloak.adminEmail
mayDiffer.KC_MOBILE_CLIENT_ID: the chart carries a working default (genie-mobile) that the realm file needs; Compose leaves it to the operator
mayDiffer.KC_MOBILE_REDIRECT_SCHEME: the chart carries a working default (genieai) that the realm file needs; Compose leaves it to the operator
mayDiffer.KC_PUBLIC_ORIGIN: the public origin, spelled from ingress.scheme + ingress.host on the chart side and from NGINX_PUBLIC_DOMAIN on the Compose side
mayDiffer.KEYCLOAK_URL: the Job reaches Keycloak in-cluster; Compose reaches it through its own service name

secretProvided.GENIE_ADMIN_PASSWORD: carried by the keycloak-admin-credentials Secret through the convergence Job's envSecrets rows

secretProvided.KC_PROXY_CLIENT_SECRET: carried by the keycloak-proxy-client-secret Secret through the convergence Job's envSecrets rows

unpaired.arango-vector-db: the chart's ArangoDB is a kube-arangodb operator custom resource, configured through the CR rather than through an environment; the operator owns the database and its creation
unpaired.certbot: the chart terminates TLS with cert-manager; there is no certbot container
unpaired.chatqna-xeon-nginx-server: the OPEA demo UI is not deployed by the chart
unpaired.chatqna-xeon-ui-server: the OPEA demo UI is not deployed by the chart
unpaired.grafana: the chart's Grafana is a grafana-operator custom resource, configured through the CR
unpaired.guardrail: the chart deploys no guardrail; the orchestrators tolerate an unreachable one and carry its default address
unpaired.keycloak: the chart's Keycloak is a keycloak-operator custom resource, configured through the CR
unpaired.kong: the chart's edge is Envoy Gateway (Gateway API), not Kong
unpaired.kong-config: the chart's edge is Envoy Gateway (Gateway API), not Kong
unpaired.kong-migrations: the chart's edge is Envoy Gateway (Gateway API), not Kong
unpaired.nginx: the chart's edge is Envoy Gateway; the standalone nginx is gone from the data path
unpaired.otel-collector: the chart's collector is an OpenTelemetry Operator custom resource, configured through the CR
unpaired.otel-collector-init: the chart ships the collector's configuration as a ConfigMap the operator consumes; there is no init container
unpaired.postgres: the chart's PostgreSQL is CloudNativePG, configured through the CR
unpaired.postgres-init: the chart's PostgreSQL is CloudNativePG; the operator creates the database and its owner
unpaired.tei: the chart's in-cluster embedding model is a Deployment whose model and endpoint come from the OPEA tier's values, not from an environment list
unpaired.tei_reranker: the chart's in-cluster reranking model is a Deployment configured through the OPEA tier's values
unpaired.tempo-proxy: the chart's traces go to the vmoperator's VMSingle, not through a tempo proxy
unpaired.textgen: the chart's in-cluster LLM is a vLLM Deployment configured through the OPEA tier's values
unpaired.victorialogs: the chart's log store is a vmoperator VMSingle custom resource
unpaired.victoriametrics: the chart's metrics store is a vmoperator VMSingle custom resource
unpaired.victoriatraces: the chart's trace store is a vmoperator VMSingle custom resource
unpaired.vllm: the chart's in-cluster LLM is a vLLM Deployment configured through the OPEA tier's values
unpaired.vllm-translation-guardrail: the chart's translation model belongs to the OPEA tier and is configured through the tier's values
